title: Incorporating AI in foreign language education: An investigation into ChatGPT’s effect on foreign language learners
extended_summary:
This paper investigates how ChatGPT affects foreign language learning experiences and how students perceive its strengths, challenges, and possible uses in language education. The authors position the study as addressing a gap in research on the practical use of generative AI in foreign language instruction, especially regarding its benefits, drawbacks, and applicability in real classroom contexts.

The intervention consisted of integrating ChatGPT into foreign language instruction over four weeks. The tool was used in online reading, writing, grammar, and vocabulary lessons, including activities such as brainstorming, creative writing, grammar practice, vocabulary work, and receiving writing feedback. Data were collected through semi-structured interviews and analyzed thematically, making this a qualitative case study rather than a controlled effectiveness trial.

The study involved 13 preparatory-class university students at a foundation university in Ankara, Turkey, during emergency distance education following a major earthquake. Participants were 18–20 years old, came from multiple departments, and had English proficiency levels from A2 to B2. One researcher also served as the language teacher implementing the activities, and the study was limited to a single classroom because university administrators only permitted implementation in one class.

The main conclusions are that students generally perceived ChatGPT as helpful for writing, grammar, and vocabulary learning, and as increasing motivation and engagement through quick feedback and flexible use. At the same time, students reported limitations, including technical problems, limited usefulness for speaking and listening, risk of overreliance, and concerns about misuse. Overall, the paper concludes that ChatGPT can be a useful supplementary tool in foreign language education, but should complement rather than replace teacher support and authentic communicative practice.
quality_tier_rationale: This is a peer-reviewed qualitative case study with a clearly described methodology, but it has a very small university sample, no comparator condition, and no direct quantitative writing-quality outcome measures. It therefore fits yellow rather than green or blue under the K-12 evidence framework.
impact_tier_rationale: Participants perceived positive effects, especially for writing-related experiences and motivation, but impact is unclear because there are no direct secondary-school writing-quality outcomes, no comparator, and no effect sizes. The study does not provide causal evidence of measurable impact.

interventions.use_case: ChatGPT was integrated into university foreign-language classes over four weeks for reading, writing, grammar, and vocabulary activities, including brainstorming essays, generating stories, practicing grammar, and giving essay feedback.
Students used ChatGPT specifically as a writing and language support tool for EFL writing improvement, grammar enhancement, vocabulary learning, and feedback on essays.

finding.finding_summary: In this qualitative case study, 13 university preparatory EFL students reported that ChatGPT positively supported writing improvement, grammar enhancement, and vocabulary learning during a 4-week intervention. Evidence is based on interview themes rather than direct pre/post writing-quality scores, and no effect sizes or statistical tests were reported.
finding.measure: Semi-structured interview reports about writing improvement, grammar enhancement, and vocabulary learning

finding.finding_summary: Students reported limited impact of ChatGPT on speaking and no impact on listening, despite perceived benefits for other language domains. These findings are based on participant perceptions from interviews, with no direct fluency assessment, effect sizes, or comparative statistics reported.
finding.measure: Semi-structured interview reports about speaking and listening impacts

finding.finding_summary: Participants generally described ChatGPT as increasing motivation and engagement in foreign-language learning, especially through instant feedback, accessibility, and varied activities, although a few students reported no motivational increase. Findings come from thematic analysis of interviews with 13 students and include no standardized engagement measures or effect sizes.
finding.measure: Semi-structured interview reports about motivation and engagement

finding.finding_summary: Students described ChatGPT as supporting creativity and idea generation in story writing and cultural exploration, but also voiced concern that it could encourage shortcuts, overreliance, and reduced learner autonomy or critical thinking. These findings are qualitative and perception-based, with no validated durable-skills instrument or effect estimates reported.
finding.measure: Semi-structured interview reports about creativity, autonomy, and shortcut-taking

finding.finding_summary: Students reported that ChatGPT made research and information access faster and more efficient during language-learning tasks. However, these efficiency gains were self-reported and were not measured with objective time-on-task or productivity metrics; no effect sizes were reported.
finding.measure: Semi-structured interview reports about time-saving and research efficiency
